title: Audit #6038 and prove a group-free four-call floor for diagonal pair targets (no new κ)
body:
## Result

**Independent audit of #6038, plus a stronger written theorem and a group-free finite certificate. No new κ.**

Subject: Nick Petalas's [PR #6038](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6038) (`research/conjugate-pair-every-group`), exact head `0cee0e104b68ce6f06bf84af03f46ac30680e64c`. It claims that in #4089's rank-one-idempotent register model, `diag([xy],[yx],[e],…,[e])` needs exactly four paid calls for every group, field and width `r ≥ 2`.

1. **Audit: no error found in #6038's PROOF.md.** I checked every step: (F1)-(F3), the corner identities, Lemmas 1-3 and all eight length-3 patterns, including that no other subset takes the value `xy` or `yx` in `xxy`/`yyx`/`xyy`/`yxx`. The model binds to #4089 over F2. Two remarks, neither affecting correctness. (F3)'s clause on `x³`/`y³` is weaker than the truth: `x³` is never `xy` or `yx`, since either would give `y = x²`. And the `xyx` case does not need the corner split. An OpenAI Codex read-only review also found no error.
2. **Theorem S (new; [PROOF.md](research/conjugate-pair-group-free-audit/PROOF.md)).** Fix distinct `a, b ≠ e`. If no label equals `a` or `b`, then `diag([a],[b],[e],…,[e])` is not a product of at most three paid calls. This holds for every label set, every coincidence among products of labels, every field and every `r ≥ 2`. The proof uses only the coefficient equations at `a`, `b` and `e`, and it has two cases. #6038's length-3 step is the special case `L = {x,y}`, `a = xy`, `b = yx`. That case needs only (F1), not (F2)/(F3) or the eight-pattern analysis. A second Codex review of this proof found no error.
3. **Group-free certificate (`verify.py`, stdlib).** #6038's finite check uses 26 coincidence keys from S3, S4, S5, Q8 and the free group. Here each subset word may take any class in `{e, xy, yx, other}` that the single equation allows. Each of the 90 equations is decided either by an S3/S4/S5 witness or by a sound cancellation rule. Joint consistency and the zero equations at other elements are dropped, so the relaxation covers every group at once. Two tiers are run: the *full* table, and a *singleton* tier that is exactly Theorem S's system. Neither has a solution of length ≤ 3 at `(r,q) = (2,2),(2,3),(2,5),(3,2)` (registered) or at `(2,7)` and `(3,3)` (local runs; the `(3,3)` run covered 1,601,613 tuples). A local `(4,2)` run timed out and is not claimed.

Controls: the direct four-call word satisfies the relaxation, and the search finds a length-4 solution on its own. Unrestricted linear algebra fits at length 2. Wrongly allowing `y = xy` reopens length 3.

## Reproduce

```sh
python3.12 -B -W error research/conjugate-pair-group-free-audit/verify.py      # ~30 s
python3.12 -O -B -W error research/conjugate-pair-group-free-audit/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/conjugate-pair-group-free-audit
python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/conjugate-pair-group-free-audit --check-source-history
```

Local results on macOS arm64, CPython 3.12: `PASS_CONJUGATE_PAIR_GROUP_FREE_AUDIT` in both modes, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`, `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Base: canonical main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`. The PR changes only its own package.

## Limits

This is a formal group-algebra statement. It covers no native address operation, conversion, restoration, caller or BIT supplier, and the selected κ (#6030) is unchanged. The finite tiers cover only small prime fields and widths; prime-power fields and `r ≥ 4` rest on the written proofs. No human or proof-kernel review is claimed.

## Open next questions

1. #6038 OQ1: is there a uniform floor of 6 for `diag([g],[h])` when neither entry is a product of at most two labels (e.g. `diag([xyx],[yxy])`)? The support-only analogue of Theorem S fails. In a local NumPy probe (not registered) at `r = 2` over F2, letting only subsets of size ≥ 3 carry `g` or `h` gives relaxed solutions at length 4 (20/1,296 tuples) and length 5 (938/7,776). So any floor of 6 must use relations among the labels. A second local probe solves the exact equations in the free group: it finds no word of length ≤ 5 for `diag([xyx],[yxy])` at r = 2 over F2, and it does find the four-call words for `(xy, yx)`. Next step: a full-tier table for the target `(xyx, yxy)`.
2. Formalize Theorem S (a short statement about rank-one matrices over a field).

## Credit

Nick Petalas (#6038) supplied the theorem audited here, the corner-sandwich method, the expansion and the direct word. Wentao Li (#4089, #4093) supplied the model and the A5/PSL(2,7) results, and Cinna Davis (#2246) the original A5 target. Theorem S, its proof, the relaxation and the verifier are new here. Prepared for Josie Elliston with substantial Claude (Anthropic) assistance; Codex was used only for review. Apache-2.0.
